pairs.question: De consummatione alicuius facti dicitur perfectio. Deus autem qui non est factus quomodo est perfectus?
pairs.answer: Sed hunc sermonem de usu nostro sumit humana inopia, sicut et reliqua uerba, quatenus id quod ineffabile est utcumque dici possit, quoniam de Deo nihil digne humanus sermo dicit.
pairs.derivation: Author poses and answers his own puzzle. Kept the preceding sentence (De consummatione... perfectio) as verbatim setup so the question's term perfectus has a referent. Answer is the full reply sentence (to its first and only full stop); nothing trimmed.

pairs.question: Quid faciebat Deus antequam caelum faceret? Cur noua uoluntas in Deo ut mundum conderet orta est?
pairs.answer: Sed noua in Deo uoluntas exorta non est, quia etsi in re mundus non erat, in aeterna tamen ratione et consilio semper erat.
pairs.derivation: Dropped the framing tag Quidam aiunt: (meta-narration of the asking). The two interrogatives are quoted objections that the author answers in his own voice. Answer is the single reply sentence to its full stop; it directly rebuts the second question and resolves both.

pairs.question: Si Deum angeli contuentur et uident, cur Petrus apostolus dicit: In quem desiderant angeli Dei conspicere? Item, si eum non contuentur, nec uident, quomodo, iuxta sententiam Domini, angeli eorum semper uident faciem Patris qui est in caelis?
pairs.answer: Sed bene utrumque est: nam ueraciter credimus quod Deum angeli et uident, et uidere desiderant; et habent, et habere festinant; et amant et amare nituntur.
pairs.derivation: Two genuine interrogatives (cur... / quomodo...) the author raises and resolves. Answer ends at the first full stop (Sed bene utrumque est... amare nituntur); the following elaboration (Si enim sic uidere desiderant...) digresses and is cut. Internal semicolons retained per the to-the-first-full-stop rule.

pairs.question: Quare non possunt animalia bruta interrogare?
pairs.derivation: Direct Quare question answered immediately by quia nesciunt ratiocinare. Cut at that point (followed in the source by a semicolon, not a full stop): what follows, ideo non dissimiles gentiles homines animalibus..., turns from answering to a digression about pagans. Capitalized the first word and supplied the terminal full stop.

pairs.question: Sed cur futura quasi praeterita scribuntur?
pairs.answer: Nisi quia ea quae adhuc facienda sunt in opere, iam facta sunt in diuina praedestinatione.
pairs.derivation: Authorial cur question with its answer in the nisi quia clause. Took the question sentence alone (intelligible on its own) rather than ellipting the preceding scriptural example. Normalized the run-on into question + answer at the natural break; capitalized Nisi and set terminal punctuation. No words added or reordered.

pairs.question: Sed cur quae adhuc facienda erant iam facta narrantur?
pairs.answer: Quia quae nobis adhuc futura sunt, apud Dei aeternitatem iam facta sunt.
pairs.derivation: From editorial-bracketed text; brackets stripped, words kept. Dropped the section-join dash between 19.14 and 19.15. Question is the cur sentence; answer is the Quia... reply to its full stop, cutting the following Quapropter... elaboration.

pairs.question: Cur paruuli peccatum originale carentes per baptismum, et necdum proprium habentes delictum, a bestiis poenisque ceteris laniantur?
pairs.answer: Haec igitur causa est: baptismum enim a poena aeterna, non a praesentis uitae supplicio liberat.
pairs.derivation: Author's Cur question answered by Haec igitur causa est... Answer ends at the first full stop; the following reasoning (quod, si a poena praesenti...) elaborates and is cut.

pairs.question: Magnitudo signorum faciet sub Antichristo ut electi, si fieri potest, in errorem mittantur. Sed si electi, quomodo sunt in errorem mittendi?
pairs.answer: Ergo ibunt in errorem titubationis ad modicum pro multitudine prodigiorum, non tamen deiciendi sunt ab stabilitate sua terrorum inpulsu atque signorum.
pairs.derivation: Kept the preceding sentence (Magnitudo signorum... mittantur) as verbatim setup so electi in the question has a referent. The interrogative (quomodo sunt in errorem mittendi?) is answered by the Ergo... sentence (to its full stop); later material (Vnde et ideo ponitur si fieri potest...) digresses and is cut.
